images.title: Between ₹45 and ₹50
images.purpose: Help students predict the size of 5 × ₹9.5 by sandwiching it between two easy whole number products.
images.composition: Three cards sit in one horizontal row across the centre, the middle card larger and highlighted; white space above and below.
exact_structure: Three rounded rectangle cards in one row, evenly spaced, centred vertically.
Middle card: larger, thick reddish purple #CC79A7 outline, text "5 × ₹9.5 = ?".
Between the left and middle card one grey #6B7280 "<" sign, and between the middle and right card one grey #6B7280 "<" sign, both drawn as plain symbols.
Below the row, one short caption line centred: "more than ₹45, less than ₹50".
No pens, no number line, no other numbers anywhere; no value written in place of the question mark.
rejection: the products 45 and 50 swapped or changed
more or fewer than three cards
the inequality signs pointing the wrong way
images.takeaway: Before multiplying, we can tell that 5 × 9.5 must lie between 45 and 50.
images.description: Three cards in a row read 5 × ₹9 = ₹45, then a highlighted 5 × ₹9.5 = ?, then 5 × ₹10 = ₹50, with less than signs between them.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text that asks students to predict the cost and keep the question in mind.
images.teaching_notes: Point from the outer cards to the middle card and ask why the answer must sit between them.

image_decisions.why: An estimate is easier to see as a sandwich between two whole number products than to read as a sentence.
